svg.title: Fig. 13(f) — Catacaustic of a circle: the radiant point near the centre
svg.desc: Redrawn from Robert C. Yates, A Handbook on Curves and Their Properties (1947), Fig. 13(f), page 16. Section: caustics.

g.data-text: The reflecting circle of radius a about O, the diameter BA and the radiant point C inside the circle on the axis.
Draw the circle about O through C. The cusps of the caustic lie on it.
At C raise the perpendicular to the axis; it cuts the given circle at T and T′. These are the points where the incident ray CT is perpendicular to OC.

With centre T and radius TC cut the circle about O again at K: K is the mirror image of C in the radius OT, so TK is the reflected ray and K is a cusp of the caustic. The same on the other side gives K′.
Draw the reflected rays TK and T′K′ and the chord KK′ perpendicular to the axis.
The caustic: from each cusp K a branch runs towards B and the two meet in a cusp near B on the axis; a short arc closes the curve on the right.
